newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. sees Hebron deal some days away.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees Hebron deal some days away.

text.p: An Israeli-Palestinian deal on a partial Israeli troop withdrawal in the West Bank town of Hebron looks to be about a week away, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

The officials, attending a Bosnia conference in Paris, said this was the assessment of U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, who stopped over for a few hours at Tel Aviv airport on Wednesday night on his way home from a Cairo conference and was briefed by U.S. officials mediating the talks.

"Dennis's appreciation is that while they made some progress this week, they clearly have a further ways to go...he doesn't believe an agreement is imminent in the next day or two," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

Burns said Ross concluded there was nothing to be gained by him staying in Israel and he proceeded on to Washington. Ross had mediated an earlier stage of the talks, but they are now being handled by U.S. ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk and consul-general to Jerusalem Edward Abington.
A senior U.S. official, speaking on condition he was not identified, said: "We think they probably have a week to go."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has cancelled a trip abroad, partly in anticipation of a deal to launch Palestinian self-rule in Hebron.
But Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Thursday Israel and the PLO had failed in late-night talks to close a deal.
"I'm sorry to say that till two o'clock this night we did not achieve any progress," Arafat told reporters in self-ruled Gaza, adding that he was "not optimistic" a deal would be signed on Thursday.
The two sides are trying to hammer out an agreement for Israel to hand over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self- rule. Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town of about 100,000 Arabs.
Palestinian officials said the sides were deadlocked over Israel's demand that its forces be allowed to enter Palestinian- controlled parts of Hebron in "hot pursuit" of suspected attackers.
